title: Game mode: Cricket for 100 (simultaneous)
goal: Add a simultaneous version of Cricket that works with up to 100 players.
details: Classic cricket uses 15-20 and the bull. With 100 players at once, closing a number cannot block 99 opponents fairly, so use 'cut-throat lite': each player marks numbers for themselves (3 marks closes a number for that player), and extra marks on a closed number score points. After 10 rounds, rank by closed numbers, then points. Bots should aim at their highest unclosed number (treble).
acceptance:
- content/modes/cricket.js implements the full mode contract
- npm test passes; the simulation finishes every game within maxRounds
- standings value shows closed numbers and points, e.g. "5 closed, 120 pts"

title: Game mode: Killer
goal: Add Killer: each player gets a number; hit your double to become a killer, then hit others' doubles to take their lives.
details: With 100 players and 20 numbers, several players share a number. Assign numbers round-robin at init using ctx.rng. Each player has 3 lives. A dart in a double removes one life from every killer-eligible opponent who owns that number (not yourself). Last player with lives wins; cap at maxRounds and then rank by lives.
acceptance:
- content/modes/killer.js implements the mode contract
- npm test passes
- The simulation report shows winners with clearly higher accuracy than the field

title: Game mode: Shanghai
goal: Add Shanghai: round N only counts hits on number N (rounds 1-7). Single+double+treble of the same number in one visit wins instantly.
details: Score = number x multiplier for hits on the round's number. A 'Shanghai' (single, double and treble of the round's number in one visit) wins immediately; if several players do it in the same round, the higher total wins. After 7 rounds the highest total wins.
acceptance:
- content/modes/shanghai.js implements the mode contract
- npm test passes

title: Game mode: Bob's 27
goal: Add Bob's 27, the doubles practice game, as a 100-player race.
details: Everyone starts with 27 points. Round N targets double N (rounds 1-20, then bull). Each hit adds 2 x N; a visit without hits subtracts 2 x N. Players at 0 or below are out. Highest score after the bull round wins.
acceptance:
- content/modes/bobs_27.js implements the mode contract
- npm test passes

title: Game mode: Halve It
goal: Add Halve It: fixed targets per round; miss the target in a visit and your score is halved.
details: Targets: 20, 16, any double, 17, any treble, 18, bull. Highest score after the last target wins.
acceptance:
- content/modes/halve_it.js implements the mode contract
- npm test passes

title: Game mode: Darts Golf (9 holes)
goal: Add Golf: hole N is number N. Double = 1 stroke, treble = 2, inner single = 3, outer single = 4, miss = 5. Lowest total after 9 holes wins.
details: Each visit is one hole; only the best dart of the visit counts (players can be assumed to 'stop' after a good dart). Inner/outer single can be told apart by distance from the centre in the dart's x/y versus the board rings.
acceptance:
- content/modes/golf.js implements the mode contract
- npm test passes

title: Game mode: Sudden Death
goal: A faster Royale: every round, everyone below the round's median score is out.
details: Ties at the median survive. If nobody would be eliminated, the single lowest visit is out (bull-off with ctx.rng on ties).
acceptance:
- content/modes/sudden_death.js implements the mode contract
- npm test passes; average game length is reported by the simulation and is clearly shorter than Royale

title: Game mode: Team Royale (10 teams of 10)
goal: Split the 100 players into 10 teams; each round the team with the lowest combined score is knocked out.
details: Assign teams with ctx.rng at init so humans are spread out. Standings: alive teams first; value shows team name and total, e.g. "Team 3 · 412". Team names can be colours.
acceptance:
- content/modes/team_royale.js implements the mode contract
- npm test passes

title: Board: Neon Night
goal: A dark, glowing board for late-night matches using the palette's blues and aquas.
details: Standard segments and rings; only the colors change. Check it in the gallery and make sure doubles and trebles are still easy to tell apart.
acceptance:
- content/boards/neon_night.json passes validation
- Readable in the gallery

title: Board: Big Bull (beginner friendly)
goal: A board with a much bigger bull and outer bull, for kids and first-timers.
details: Keep the 20 standard numbers so every mode can be played on it. Respect the validator's minimum ring gaps.
acceptance:
- content/boards/big_bull.json passes validation
- Simulation shows shorter Around the Clock games than on Classic

title: Board: Pro Thin Rings
goal: A hard board with thin trebles and doubles for the experts.
details: Use the minimum allowed ring widths. Standard numbers.
acceptance: - content/boards/pro_thin.json passes validation

title: Board: Clock Order (1-20 clockwise)
goal: A silly board where the numbers simply run 1 to 20 clockwise. Makes Around the Clock trivially easy and Royale strangely different.
details: Segments [1..20]. Pick a cheerful color scheme.
acceptance: - content/boards/clock_order.json passes validation

title: Tests: unit tests for the 501 checkout brain
goal: Make sure bots in 501 never aim at a target that busts them on the first dart.
details: For every remaining score 2..501, check that x01's aim() returns a target whose score does not leave 1 or below zero, and that even numbers <= 40 aim at the matching double.
acceptance: - test/x01.test.mjs exists and passes with node --test

title: Tests: property tests for board scoring
goal: Check that aimPoint() of every number/ring on every board scores exactly that number/ring.
details: Loop over all boards in content/boards and every segment number with rings single, double, treble, plus bull and outer bull.
acceptance: - test/board-properties.test.mjs exists and passes

title: Core: show each player's last darts when hovering their row
goal: Hovering a name in the field list highlights that player's darts on the board.
details: The snapshot already contains visits for everyone. Add a highlighted set to the board view.
acceptance:
- Works with mouse; on touch, tapping a row toggles the highlight
- npm test passes

title: Core: Dutch translation of the game UI
goal: Add a tiny i18n layer and a Dutch translation, selectable in the menu.
details: Keep it dependency-free: a game/ui/i18n.js with an English and a Dutch string table. Content (player bios etc.) stays as written.
acceptance:
- All UI strings in game/index.html and game/main.js come from the table
- Language choice is remembered (try/catch around localStorage)

title: Core: sound effects (thunk, crowd, elimination)
goal: Add synthesized sounds with the WebAudio API (no audio files) and a mute toggle.
details: A short 'thunk' when a dart lands, a cheer on 100+ visits, a sad trombone when you are eliminated.
acceptance:
- game/ui/sound.js, mute toggle remembered
- No sound before the first user interaction

title: Core: keyboard aiming for accessibility
goal: Let players aim with the arrow keys and throw with space.
details: Arrow keys move the aim point by 5mm (shift: 20mm). Space throws. Announce each dart's score in an aria-live region.
acceptance:
- Playable without a mouse
- npm test passes

title: Core: emoji reactions in online rooms
goal: Let people in an online room send one of six emoji reactions that float over everyone's board.
details: Rate limit to one reaction per 2 seconds per player on the server. Fixed emoji set; no free text (no moderation needed).
acceptance:
- New POST /api/rooms/:code/react endpoint with validation
- Reactions appear for all players via the event stream

title: Core: test the multiplayer server end-to-end
goal: Add an automated test that starts the server on a random port, creates a room, joins a second player, plays two rounds and checks the snapshots.
details: Use node:test and fetch; read the SSE stream manually. ROUND_SECONDS and RESULTS_MS can be lowered with environment variables.
acceptance: - test/server.test.mjs passes and cleans up after itself
